name: Salvage-Mere
specific_features: Starship crash site: the freighter Cormorant's Hoard went down intact during a runaway storm while fleeing customs cutters, and now rests upright on the seafloor at nine hundred meters, her cargo manifest listing platinum bullion and one vault sealed under an unregistered corporate seal.

Automated beacon: a storm-rider buoy network left by the freighter's insurers still marks the wreck site and logs every vessel that approaches, transmitting the ledger to an address that no longer exists.
description: A single world-ocean wraps Salvage-Mere in deep indigo, broken only by volcanic shoals where the water glows with rings of blue-green microbial light. Storm cells the size of continents crawl slowly across the surface, and between them the sea lies flat as poured glass. From orbit, the bioluminescent blooms trace slow spirals like a fingerprint turning in the dark.

Under dense air and low gravity, swells run tall and unhurried, and sound carries for miles across open water. Sailors describe the night sea as warm breath against the hull, lit from below by drifting lantern-chains of microbes. When a storm passes, the whole ocean smells faintly of ozone and crushed herbs.

Forty years ago the freighter Cormorant's Hoard chose the deep over a customs blockade and has been the most expensive shipwreck on any chart since. Her manifest is public record; the contents of her sealed aft vault are not. Divers who have reached the hull report a rhythmic tapping from inside the vault, spaced exactly like someone knocking back.

Insurance syndicates, salvage guilds, and two governments all claim the wreck, and each hires crews to beat the others to it. The knocking has grown louder as the years pass, and last season the buoy network logged an approach by something moving far too fast to be a diver. Whatever the Cormorant's Hoard was carrying, it may not care to stay carried.
